children: U.K. growth figures are overstating the true pace of economic growth, James Smith at ING says. GDP grew stronger than expected for the second month in a row in July. However, the IT sector did a lot of the heavy lifting, which makes up only 7% of economic output, Smith says. Economic performance also tends to be stronger in the first half of the year than the second. Growth has undeniably held up better than expected at the start of the war in Iran. But a lot of that comes down to inflation not rising as much as it could have done, Smith says. "How much longer that can continue, in an environment of rising energy prices and a fragile jobs market, is debatable." (don.forbes@wsj.com)
